summary: Onboarding tour (backend and front-end wiring): a read-only-for-the-person's-data demo project (pdh-demo) served from a throw-away offline SQLite sandbox built from a built-in fixture (29 public arXiv Transformer-lineage papers: 5 unrated candidates + 24 earlier records spread over four weeks, with categories, pinned-term history and pre-written zh/en previews); request routing by header X-PDH-Demo or project_id with an allow list and a 403 demo_readonly for everything else; /api/onboarding (state, start, done) with state in onboarding.json; /api/projects carries a demo descriptor; app_version.current(); first-run assertions in the packaged-backend verifier. Front end: tour.js/tour.css wired into the main, settings, weekly and creation pages; api() sends the demo header only while the demo is current; the demo id is never stored; demo mode hides every entry that would fetch, call a model, read a PDF or edit; settings 'replay tour'; creation page offers 'see the demo' when there is no project. Later in the same unit: a bilingual welcome card (w0) before the tour chooses interface language and appearance (saved with merge so other settings survive; the demo sandbox is built after the save so it follows the language); the daily button no longer names a number; not interested / too hard show a pressed state on cards and in the detail pane, are undone by pressing again (/api/undo by record id; /api/feedback retract), and survive a reload (cards carry feedback, feedback_id, familiarity; every feedback write returns the stored state).

open_risks: The organization worker lock is global: a demo graph job and a real organization job exclude each other (the loser gets 'already running').
A request that sends X-PDH-Demo gets the sandbox for every non-settings route; the page must send the header only while the tour is on screen.
Windows cannot delete an open sandbox file; the old generation then stays until the next reset (tested by simulating a failed delete, not on Windows).
Direction names in the sandbox library are written in the language chosen at reset time; switching the interface language mid-tour does not rename them.
